key_insight: BudgetMem introduces a runtime, query-aware budget-tier routing mechanism that dynamically selects which memories to access per query, giving explicit control over the performance–cost trade-off while preserving query-critical information.
problem_solved: Addresses inefficiency and information loss from offline, query-agnostic memory construction in LLM agents and the high overhead / poor cost-control of prior runtime memory methods.
method: Query-aware routing: a lightweight controller scores incoming queries and routes relevant memory items into budgeted access tiers (e.g., hot/warm/cold) per query.
Budget-tier design: memories are organized into tiers with explicit compute/latency budgets to trade off retrieval depth and cost.
Low-overhead runtime policy: an adaptive retrieval and storage pipeline that enforces budget constraints, prioritizes query-critical information, and reduces unnecessary accesses.
impact: Allows AI practitioners to run LLM agents that use memory more efficiently and predictably—reducing latency and compute cost without sacrificing task performance—while providing explicit knobs to tune the cost-performance trade-off.
visual_elements: Architecture flow: query → routing controller → tiered memory (hot/warm/cold) → retrieval, showing decision points and budgets.
Cost vs. performance chart: Pareto curve comparing BudgetMem to offline and prior runtime baselines.
Tiered memory diagram: visual of memory items sorted into budgets (hot = expensive/high-relevance, cold = cheap/low-relevance).
Example timeline: single query lifecycle highlighting which memories were selected, stored, or pruned under a given budget.
paper_title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
paper_authors: Haozhen Zhang, Haodong Yue, Tao Feng, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao
